# Round two {#sec-round-two}

Following structured group discussions of Round 1 discrepancies (@sec-round-one), all interpreters revised their assignments in **Round 2** [@Hemming_2018; @IUCN_2025]. Round 2 includes five interpreters (`Adelina_Latinovic`, `Anne Kitchener`, `David_Keith`, `Jayne_Balmer`, and `Mark_Tozer`), and every interpreter assessed the complete set of **153 eligible TASVEG 5.0 communities**. Because Round 2 incorporates both shared conceptual clarification and full coverage across all five interpreters, it forms the basis for the synthesis and spatial outputs in Part III (@sec-synthesis–@sec-maps).

:::{.aside}

Our setup for this R session loads `ecoSynthesis`, tidyverse/plotting packages, custom plot styling, and the validated lookup and membership tables:

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ecoSynthesis)
library(ggplot2)
here::i_am("analysis/round-2.qmd")
output_dir <- here::here("../results/XREFs")
source(here::here("../scripts/setup.R"))
source(here::here("../scripts/functions.R"))
load(here::here(output_dir, "lookup-tables.rda"))
load(here::here(output_dir, "memb-tables.rda"))
```

:::

## Filtering Round 2 and building the 3D membership matrix

We filter `TASVEG_clean` to Round 2 and construct the 3D `membership_matrix` (`[source, target, interpreter]`) via `ecoSynthesis::membership_matrix()`. Notice that all 5 interpreters now have 153 assessed source units across 31 candidate EFGs (compared with 29 EFGs in Round 1), and `Mark_Tozer`'s split `T4.5` entry for `SWR` (@sec-exploration) is summed automatically inside the matrix:

```{r}
TASVEG_revised <- filter(TASVEG_clean, round == 2)
TASVEG_mtx_r2 <- membership_matrix(TASVEG_revised)
TASVEG_mtx_r2
```

We can inspect an individual slice of the 3D array using `unclass()`—for example, the first four TASVEG units across the first six target EFGs for `Adelina_Latinovic`:

```{r}
unclass(TASVEG_mtx_r2)[1:4, 1:6, "Adelina_Latinovic"]
```

## Inter-interpreter agreement (`calc_agreement`)

### Global agreement between interpreter pairs

Calling `calc_agreement(TASVEG_mtx_r2)` computes global pairwise agreement across all 10 unique interpreter pairs (mirrored symmetrically with diagonal = 1). Compared to Round 1 (@sec-round-one), every pair of interpreters now compares all 153 units and achieves substantially higher mean similarity ($\ge 0.84$ across every pair):

```{r}
ag2_global <- calc_agreement(TASVEG_mtx_r2)
ag2_global
```

The heatmap below visualises the global Round 2 pairwise similarity matrix:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 5.5
ggplot(ag2_global, aes(x = interpreter_x, y = interpreter_y, fill = mean_similarity)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_text(
        aes(
            label = sprintf("%.2f\n(%.0f%% id.)", mean_similarity, 100 * share_identical),
            colour = mean_similarity > 0.88
        ),
        size = 3.2
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = teal_low, high = teal_high, limits = c(0.75, 1)) +
    label_colour_scale +
    labs(
        title = "Round 2: Mean pairwise similarity and share of identical profiles",
        x = NULL,
        y = NULL,
        fill = "Mean similarity"
    ) +
    coord_fixed() +
    theme_wp3() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1))
```

### Per-unit pairwise dissimilarity

Next, `calc_agreement(TASVEG_mtx_r2, by_source = TRUE)` computes pairwise similarity and dissimilarity for all 1,530 unit-pair combinations (153 units × 10 interpreter pairs). The faceted histograms illustrate the strong concentration near $S = 1$ across all ten pairs:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
ag2_by_source <- calc_agreement(TASVEG_mtx_r2, by_source = TRUE)

ggplot(ag2_by_source, aes(x = similarity)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, fill = teal_high, colour = "white") +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(interpreter_x), cols = vars(interpreter_y)) +
    labs(
        title = "Round 2: Distribution of pairwise similarity by interpreter pair",
        x = "Pairwise similarity (1 - dissimilarity)",
        y = "Number of TASVEG units"
    ) +
    theme_wp3()
```

Summarising `ag2_by_source` by `source` identifies how many TASVEG communities achieved complete consensus across all five interpreters in Round 2, lists the 10 remaining most-contested units, and plots the unit-level dissimilarity distribution:

```{r}
unit_disagreement_r2 <- ag2_by_source |>
    group_by(VEGCODE = source) |>
    summarise(
        mean_dissimilarity = mean(dissimilarity),
        min_dissimilarity = min(dissimilarity),
        max_dissimilarity = max(dissimilarity),
        n_pairs = n(),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(desc(mean_dissimilarity), VEGCODE)

message(sprintf(
    "%s of %s units have identical profiles from every interpreter in Round 2.",
    sum(unit_disagreement_r2$max_dissimilarity < 0.001),
    nrow(unit_disagreement_r2)
))

head(unit_disagreement_r2, 10)

ggplot(unit_disagreement_r2, aes(x = mean_dissimilarity)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, fill = rust_high, colour = "white") +
    labs(
        title = "Round 2: Mean pairwise dissimilarity across TASVEG units",
        x = "Mean pairwise dissimilarity per unit",
        y = "Number of TASVEG units"
    ) +
    theme_wp3()
```

## Target usage patterns across interpreters

Using `ecoSynthesis::membership_target_heatmap()` and `ecoSynthesis::membership_target_pair_heatmap()` on `TASVEG_revised` shows how evenly the 31 candidate EFGs are used across all five interpreters and ten interpreter pairs after group discussion:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 8.5
membership_target_heatmap(TASVEG_revised) +
    labs(title = "Round 2 Target Use")
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8.5
membership_target_pair_heatmap(TASVEG_revised) +
    labs(title = "Round 2 Shared Target Use")
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Package caveat: hardcoded plot titles in `ecoSynthesis` v0.0.0.9005
Both `membership_target_heatmap()` (default `"Round X Target Use"`) and `membership_target_pair_heatmap()` (default `"Round 1 Shared Target Use"`) hardcode their plot titles and do not yet accept a `round` filter in `v0.0.0.9005`. Pre-filtering to `round == 2` and appending `+ ggplot2::labs(title = ...)` ensures accurate Round 2 labels without modifying package code.
:::

## Within-interpreter uncertainty: Shannon's entropy

We next compute normalised Shannon's entropy for Round 2 using `ecoSynthesis::calc_entropy_tbl()` across the entire dataset (`overall`), per interpreter (`by_interpreter`), per TASVEG community (`by_source`), and per target EFG (`by_target`).

::: {.callout-note}
## Incomplete-sum warning on `HSE`
Recall from @sec-exploration that `Jayne_Balmer`'s Round 2 profile for `HSE` sums to `0.90`. When `calc_entropy_tbl()` calls `calc_shannons_entropy()` on that vector, `ecoSynthesis` emits an informative warning (`sum of the probabilities is less than 1 (0.9)`) and automatically re-normalises the non-zero probabilities internally ($p_k / \sum p$) so entropy remains strictly comparable on $[0, 1]$.
:::

```{r}
calc_entropy_tbl(TASVEG_revised, overall = "overall")
calc_entropy_tbl(TASVEG_revised, overall = "by_interpreter")
```

Inspecting the highest-entropy source units and target EFGs highlights communities that interpreters consistently view as ecologically transitional or multi-functional (for example, woodland/forest ecotones or palustrine wetlands):

```{r}
ent2_by_source <- calc_entropy_tbl(TASVEG_revised, overall = "by_source")
head(ent2_by_source, 10)

calc_entropy_tbl(TASVEG_revised, overall = "by_target") |>
    head(10)

ggplot(ent2_by_source, aes(x = mean_by_source_entropy_source_normalised)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, fill = "#355C7D", colour = "white") +
    labs(
        title = "Round 2: Mean source-normalised Shannon's entropy across units",
        x = "Mean source-normalised entropy",
        y = "Number of TASVEG units"
    ) +
    theme_wp3()
```

## Inspecting the most contested Round 2 units

Finally, we inspect the two units with the largest remaining pairwise disagreement in Round 2 (`FMG` and `SWR`) using `membership_tile_plot()`, overriding the default title to reflect Round 2:

```{r}
TASVEG |>
    dplyr::filter(VEGCODE == "FMG") |>
    dplyr::glimpse()

dplyr::filter(TASVEG_revised, VEGCODE == "FMG") |>
    membership_tile_plot() +
    labs(title = "Round 2 Cross-Referencing")
```

```{r}
TASVEG |>
    dplyr::filter(VEGCODE == "SWR") |>
    dplyr::glimpse()

dplyr::filter(TASVEG_revised, VEGCODE == "SWR") |>
    membership_tile_plot() +
    labs(title = "Round 2 Cross-Referencing")
```
